entries.claim: GEO increases visibility by 40%
entries.circulation: Unqualified retellings of the GEO headline; our earlier quotable-numbers reading, withdrawn November 3, 2026
entries.primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
entries.primary_finding: GEO experiment: Aggarwal et al. (KDD 2024) headline a gain of up to 40% in a position-adjusted word-count visibility metric. Treat it as fragile: the ICLR 2024 draft reported 37%, the paper's own five-seed rerun (appendix Table 6) gives 36.9%, and on Perplexity adding citations cut the judged score by 23% (19.0 vs 24.7) while keyword stuffing raised it 14%. It is not a citation, traffic or conversion gain. We have not recovered the exact ICLR submission for an independent check of the reported 37% headline. That version comparison remains a reported historical claim, not a newly verified result.
entries.base_setting: 1,000-query test split; five supplied source documents per query; 2024 publication
entries.quotable_correction: The GEO headline remains fragile, source-specific experimental evidence, not a citation, traffic or conversion gain.

entries.claim: The ICLR draft headline is 37%
entries.circulation: Aggarwal et al., GEO
entries.primary_source: Aggarwal et al., GEO; retrieved arXiv versions 1 and 2, https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735v1 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735v2
entries.source_location: Abstracts; exact ICLR submission not recovered
entries.primary_finding: Both retrieved arXiv abstracts print up to 40%. We have not recovered the exact ICLR submission needed to check the separate 37% headline. The versions cannot be silently substituted.
entries.base_setting: Version audit, not a new effect estimate
entries.quotable_correction: The 37% version comparison is unverified until its exact submission is identified.

entries.claim: Keyword stuffing makes you 15% less likely to be cited
entries.circulation: Unqualified marketing retelling
entries.primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
entries.primary_finding: In the 200-example supplied-file Perplexity test, judged impression is 28.1 for stuffing versus 24.7 baseline, about 13.8% higher. Source addition is 19.0, about 23.1% lower. Position-adjusted word count is a different outcome and does decline for stuffing.
entries.base_setting: 200 test examples supplied as files; 2024 paper; judged impression and position-adjusted word count must remain separate
entries.quotable_correction: The GEO paper reports metric-specific results, not a universal penalty in citation probability.

entries.claim: Structured data adds 40% visibility
entries.circulation: Abu Rayhan report and derivative GEO claims
entries.primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
entries.source_location: Tested methods in section 2.2.2 and Table 1
entries.primary_finding: The original GEO experiment does not contain a structured-data treatment. Its quotation-addition result cannot be relabeled as a schema effect.
entries.base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
entries.quotable_correction: The original GEO benchmark did not test a structured-data uplift.

entries.claim: The International Chocolate Consumption Research Group is a research source

entries.claim: Source citations outperform quotations in the original GEO table

entries.quotable_correction: In GEO Table 1, quotation addition exceeds statistics addition, which exceeds source addition, on the specified score.

entries.claim: Authoritative tone gives no significant improvement
entries.circulation: GEO results text
entries.primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3

entries.base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
entries.quotable_correction: The paper pairs a no-significant-improvement statement with positive table estimates; quote both and do not invent a significance result.

entries.claim: AutoGEO improves performance up to 50.99%
entries.circulation: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1

entries.primary_finding: The three Overall gains over Fluency are approximately 48.1%, 47.2% and 57.7%; their mean is about 51.0%. The largest of those gains is about 57.7%, rather than 51.0%.

entries.quotable_correction: The AutoGEO headline corresponds to an average across three settings, not the maximum.

entries.quotable_correction: The 35.99% figure averages two rewrite variants across three benchmark settings on one experimental engine; it is not a cross-engine field effect.

entries.claim: AutoGEO rule overlap is exactly 40.00% in the stated cross-domain setting
entries.circulation: AutoGEO v 1 Figure 2
entries.primary_source: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1
entries.source_location: Figure 2 b, section 5.3 and Tables 7 to 8, PDF pages 15 to 16
entries.primary_finding: The printed keyword labels give 17 Researchy-GEO, 15 GEO-Bench and 14 e-commerce labels. Their first two Jaccard overlaps reproduce 88.24% and 34.78%. GEO-Bench versus e-commerce shares 7 labels in a union of 22, giving 31.82%, rather than the printed 40.00%. This is a label-set reconstruction, not a reconstruction of latent rule meaning.
entries.base_setting: Three printed keyword sets in AutoGEO preprint version 1
entries.quotable_correction: The printed keyword sets reproduce two overlaps but give 31.82%, not 40.00%, for the remaining pair.

entries.source_location: Sections 6.4 and 6.6, mention bands and sentiment eligibility

entries.claim: The worked review scores reproduce from the stated normalized formula
entries.circulation: Roumeliotis et al. 2026 Table 1
entries.primary_source: Roumeliotis et al. (2026), The Evolution of SEO in the Era of Generative AI, Electronics 15, 3541, DOI 10.3390/electronics15163541
entries.source_location: Equations 1 and 2, Table 1, pages 6 to 7; independent upper-bound arithmetic
entries.primary_finding: Under the stated six normalized weighted criteria and the visible raw maxima, the example upper bounds are approximately 0.792, 0.650 and 0.587, below printed 0.89, 0.84 and 0.61. The text also mentions a DOI bonus without showing how it enters the normalized equation. The published recipe therefore does not reproduce its worked scores.
entries.base_setting: Three worked examples; weights 0.40/0.25/0.15/0.10/0.05/0.05; additional DOI-bonus handling unspecified
entries.quotable_correction: The review needs a reproducible normalization and bonus calculation before its worked scores can be verified.

entries.claim: Uniformly changing every score weight by 10% changes the ranking
entries.circulation: Roumeliotis et al. 2026 sensitivity analysis
entries.primary_source: Roumeliotis et al. (2026), The Evolution of SEO in the Era of Generative AI, Electronics 15, 3541, DOI 10.3390/electronics15163541
entries.primary_finding: Multiplying every fixed weight by the same positive constant preserves every pairwise score order. The reported 54.3% to 80.0% overlaps do not give per-scenario results reconciling the uniform cases or additional manual changes.
entries.base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
entries.quotable_correction: Uniform positive rescaling of fixed weights cannot change the score ranking; the stated sensitivity analysis needs further explanation.
